questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found it important that there was courses on the university within a field that I found interesting. However, I also went on exchange to explore new cultures and have a personal experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The administrative burden by going on exchange is what is making my rate an 8 instead of a 10. I had problems with the online platform for making the learning agreement - the text on the website was confusing and my receiving university did not receive it to sign, so I had to send it manually. Another irritation was that I had to make proof of arrival and departure for both receiving and sending university, instead of having a shared formular or something.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I did not have problems there. I had issues at the receiving university with choosing courses, as it had to be done over emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Email-correspondence.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. I ended up renting an airbnb (to different places in order to have accommodation for the whole period). That was very expensive, but I had no other solutions.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Start searching as soon as possible, and be open...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were no housing or help provided by the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It had to be done over email-correspondence, and it was difficult to figure out which courses I was eligible to join. It was very stressful during the period.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to send emails to an office that then answered and enrolled you in courses. There was many emails back and forth in order to get figure out which courses, that i was eligible to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Emails

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 1 out of 3 courses that I wanted. The other were ok, but not what I had expected.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient and write emails.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Academic level was good, but less empirical. The applied courses were very easy compared to home university.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1) Contemporary Debates in Media Sociology 2) Understanding Empire 3) Quantitative Methods in the Social Sciences

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Contemporarty Debates in Media Sociology and Understanding Empire were two good courses. The methods course was very beginner level.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Remember to set aside money for small trips to the countryside, and for other weekend-activities.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Accommodation was way more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything! All kind of sports-clubs and also cultural clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the Walking Society for going on hikes in the Scottish nature. I also recommend joining the Mature Students Association. A mature student in Glasgow is 23+, and for a small membership fee, you get access to a reading room, kitchen and other stuff in a small cool clubhouse at the university grounds.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the highlands! Especially Isle of Skye, Glencoe, Loch Lomond and the rest of the West Highlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a club or talk to people in your class.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was not really any challenges. Scottish people are very friendly and easy-going.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pub-culture. Go to a pub-quiz, small concert or just have a pint at the pub.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start searching for accommodation as quickly as possible!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to go to some activities during Fresher's Week that is the intro-period at Glasgow Uni. That is where you might make new friends.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Enjoying Scotland. Both the people and the Nature is some of the best in the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accomodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
